text.content:
The corridor widens into a rough gallery, and through a gap in the crumbling wall to the south the party can see straight into the Larders beyond: a genuine throne assembled entirely from stacked, buckled saddlebags, and, curled contentedly atop the highest one, wearing a crude circlet woven from raw wool, a llama who is very clearly the point of everyone's attention.

GM Notes

Milestone: This is the party's first real look at the Wool-Crowned Warrens' actual power structure - and it's genuinely ambiguous from here whether the llama or the goblin standing beside the throne is really in charge. Let the players form their own theory before the Boss Arena (Room 28) resolves it: the llama, Buttercup, is a beloved figurehead the goblins sincerely worship; the goblin, Corvin Blackwell, is the one actually pulling every lever, and increasingly not a goblin anymore in any way that matters.

Say/show: Describe Corvin at a distance if he's visible: ashen skin, small dark horns, eyes that don't quite track normally - a shape that used to be goblin-sized and goblin-shaped and isn't settled on staying that way. Nobody in the room reacts to this as strange.

Hazard/route note: There is no way through the gap itself (it's a sightline, not a passage) - the actual route to the Larders continues via the corridor spine (Rooms 8/17/18).
